-health-check.name: -health-check
-health-check.description: Internal health check. The webhook trigger needs no credentials; if a MAKE_API_TOKEN is configured, validates it against the Make account API. For full scenario management, the token should have scopes: scenarios:read, scenarios:write, teams:read, organizations:read.

trigger-webhook.name: trigger-webhook
trigger-webhook.description: Trigger a Make.com scenario by POSTing a JSON payload to its webhook URL. No account token required — the user supplies the webhook URL (https://hook.<region>.make.com/<token>). Returns { delivered, statusCode, webhookHost, region, responseType, response }.

params.webhookUrl: The Make.com webhook URL (https://hook.<region>.make.com/<token>). Only *.make.com hosts over https are accepted.
params.payload: Body sent to the webhook. A JSON object is sent as application/json; a string is forwarded as-is (JSON string → application/json, otherwise text/plain).

list-scenarios.name: list-scenarios
list-scenarios.description: List Make.com scenarios for the configured account (requires MAKE_API_TOKEN in user secrets). Optionally filter by teamId and page with limit/offset. Returns { scenarios: [{ id, name, isActive, isPaused, teamId }], returned, total, offset, limit, hasMore, nextOffset, teamId, region }. When hasMore is true, call again with offset=nextOffset to fetch the next page.

params.teamId: Make team id to scope the scenarios (found in the team URL). Required by the Make API on most accounts.
params.limit: Max scenarios to return per page (1-100, default 50).
params.offset: Number of scenarios to skip for pagination (default 0). Pass the `nextOffset` from a previous response to fetch the next page.
params.includeRaw: Include the unprocessed upstream scenario rows under `raw` for debugging (default false).

run-scenario.name: run-scenario
run-scenario.description: Run a Make.com scenario on demand by id (requires MAKE_API_TOKEN in user secrets). Pass optional `data` for the run inputs and `responsive: true` to wait for and return its outputs. Returns { scenarioId, executionId, status, responsive, outputs }.

params.scenarioId: The id of the scenario to run (from list-scenarios).
params.data: Optional input data passed to the scenario run.
params.responsive: If true, wait for the run to finish and return its outputs (default false).

create-scenario.name: create-scenario
create-scenario.description: Create a new Make.com scenario (requires MAKE_API_TOKEN in user secrets). The `blueprint` is provided as a JSON object and is serialized internally. Returns { scenarioId, name, teamId, folderId, isActive, region, url }. Some Make plans require a paid subscription to use this endpoint.

params.teamId: Make team id that will own the scenario.
params.name: Human-readable name for the scenario.
params.blueprint: Scenario blueprint as a JSON object (not an escaped string). It will be serialized to a string before sending to Make.
params.scheduling: Scheduling configuration. Defaults to { type: "indefinitely", interval: 60 }.
params.folderId: Optional folder id to place the scenario in.
params.confirmed: Whether the scenario is confirmed on creation (default true).
params.basedon: Optional id of an existing scenario to base this one on.

get-scenario.name: get-scenario
get-scenario.description: Get a single Make.com scenario by id (requires MAKE_API_TOKEN in user secrets). Returns the scenario object as returned by Make.

params.scenarioId: The id of the scenario to retrieve.

get-scenario-blueprint.name: get-scenario-blueprint
get-scenario-blueprint.description: Get the blueprint of a Make.com scenario by id (requires MAKE_API_TOKEN in user secrets). Returns { scenarioId, blueprint } where blueprint is a parsed JSON object when possible.

params.scenarioId: The id of the scenario whose blueprint to retrieve.

update-scenario.name: update-scenario
update-scenario.description: Update an existing Make.com scenario by id (requires MAKE_API_TOKEN in user secrets). Supports updating name, blueprint (as a JSON object), scheduling, and folderId. Returns the updated scenario summary.

params.scenarioId: The id of the scenario to update.
params.name: New name for the scenario.
params.blueprint: New scenario blueprint as a JSON object (not an escaped string). It will be serialized to a string before sending to Make.
params.folderId: New folder id for the scenario.

delete-scenario.name: delete-scenario
delete-scenario.description: Delete a Make.com scenario by id (requires MAKE_API_TOKEN in user secrets). This action is irreversible. Returns { scenarioId, deleted, region }.

params.scenarioId: The id of the scenario to delete.

clone-scenario.name: clone-scenario
clone-scenario.description: Clone an existing Make.com scenario by id (requires MAKE_API_TOKEN in user secrets). Optionally set a new name or folder. Returns the cloned scenario summary.

params.scenarioId: The id of the scenario to clone.
params.name: Optional new name for the cloned scenario.
params.folderId: Optional folder id for the cloned scenario.

start-scenario.name: start-scenario
start-scenario.description: Activate (start) a Make.com scenario by id (requires MAKE_API_TOKEN in user secrets). Returns { scenarioId, isActive, region }.

params.scenarioId: The id of the scenario to activate.

stop-scenario.name: stop-scenario
stop-scenario.description: Pause (stop) a Make.com scenario by id (requires MAKE_API_TOKEN in user secrets). Returns { scenarioId, isActive, region }.

params.scenarioId: The id of the scenario to pause.

name: Make
description: Make.com automation — trigger scenarios via webhooks (no token needed) and manage scenarios via the account API: create, read, update, delete, clone, start, stop, list, run, and inspect blueprints.
